items.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 11:34AM PDT until October 22 at 1:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues. Canyon rock
and mud slides possible.

* WHERE...Southeastern Santa Barbara County in southwestern
California...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Canyon rock and mud slides possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1134 AM PDT, Doppler radar and rain gauges indicated heavy
rain due to scattered showers and thunderstorms. Minor flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area.
Canyon rock and mud slides possible.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Santa Barbara, Montecito, Carpinteria, Summerland, Rincon Point,
La Conchita, Goleta, Mission Canyon and Hope Ranch.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

items.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 21 at 10:08AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
A moderate storm system will impact our coastal waters today
through Thursday, bringing a chance of thunderstorms to the area.
Thunderstorm activity is likely to be most hazardous for the
waters south and east of Point Conception with peak timing
expected this afternoon through Thursday morning.

Any thunderstorm that forms will be capable of producing local
gusts up to gale force, rough seas, dangerous lightning, heavy
rainfall with reduced visibility, and waterspouts.
